# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 2

**1** After she had finished speaking she said to me, "Do you wish to hear me read?" "Yes, lady," I said. "Listen then," she said. She opened the little book and read to me, not from the beginning, but from something in the middle, and she said: **2** "Behold, O God of powers, who by your invisible great might and by your abundant wisdom created the world and by your glorious purpose clothed your creation with loveliness, and by your strong word fixed the heavens and founded the earth upon the waters, and by your own wisdom and providence formed your holy church, which you also blessed — **3** Behold, he removes the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas, and all things will be made level for his elect, so that he may fulfill to them the promise he made with great glory and joy, if they keep the ordinances of God which they received in great faith." **4** When she finished the reading, I arose and said, "Lady, what does it mean that the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas are removed?" She said to me, "Each of these things, when it is removed, must needs do service for the elect of God. For all the mountains and the hills and the seas and the heavens are as enemies of the elect, and they shall be removed. Then those who are faithful and single-hearted shall enjoy the good things, but those who are wicked shall not enter in." **5** She said to me, "I will show you that it is I alone who am all things — patience and love and truth, and the foundation of the saints and their building up and their wall and their tower and their power." I said to her, "Lady, show me what you mean." She said to me, "Do you not see before you a great tower being built upon the water, with bright squared stones?"

---

*EMET note: The tower is introduced here at the close of Vision 2, to be elaborated in Vision 3. "Single-hearted" renders haplous/simple = those who are not double-minded.*
